Plato on education

Plato (c. 428/427–348/347 BCE) approaches education within Platonism. Plato’s theory of Forms holds that changing sensibles participate in eternal, intelligible paradigms—Justice, Beauty, Equality—crowned by the Form of the Good. Knowledge differs from mere opinion by grasping these stable realities through dialectic and recollection. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets education most directly—useful for searches such as “plato quotes on education.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the Plato thinker page for biography and to the education theme for other voices on the same question.
